UserProfile.title: UserProfile
UserProfile.description: Represents a user's profile in the Game of Gyan application, including progress and personal information.

id.description: Unique identifier for the UserProfile entity, matching the Firebase Auth UID.

level.description: Current calculated level of the user based on XP.

xp.description: Total experience points of the user.

streak.description: Current learning streak of the user in days.

avatarUrl.description: URL of the user's chosen avatar image.

completedCourses.description: An array of IDs for courses the user has completed.

completedLevels.description: An array of IDs for individual course levels the user has completed.

completedExpertChallenges.description: An array of IDs for expert-level challenges the user has completed.

completedHardChallenges.description: An array of IDs for 'Find the Error' challenges the user has completed.

Course.title: Course
Course.description: Represents a coding course offered on the platform.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Course entity.

name.description: Name of the course (e.g., Python Basics).

language.description: Programming language covered by the course (e.g., Python, Java).

levelIds.description: References to Levels within the course. (Relationship: Course 1:N Level)

Level.title: Level
Level.description: Represents a level within a specific coding course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Level entity.

courseId.description: Reference to the Course this level belongs to. (Relationship: Course 1:N Level)

name.description: Name of the level (e.g., Level 1, Introduction).

order.description: Order of the level within the course.

gameIds.description: References to Games within this level. (Relationship: Level 1:N Game)

Game.title: Game
Game.description: Represents a game or exercise within a coding level.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Game entity.

levelId.description: Reference to the Level this game belongs to. (Relationship: Level 1:N Game)

type.description: Type of the game (e.g., MCQ, Fill-in-the-blanks, Drag-and-drop).

correctAnswer.description: The correct answer to the game

xpReward.description: XP points awarded for completing the game.

Badge.title: Badge
Badge.description: Represents a badge earned by a user.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Badge entity.

name.description: Name of the badge (e.g., First Steps, Code Master).

description.description: Description of the badge and how to earn it.

Certificate.title: Certificate
Certificate.description: Represents a certificate earned by a user upon completing a course.

id.description: Unique identifier for the Certificate entity.

userProfileId.description: Reference to the UserProfile who earned the certificate. (Relationship: UserProfile 1:N Certificate)

courseId.description: Reference to the Course completed to earn the certificate. (Relationship: Course 1:N Certificate)

completionDate.description: Date when the course was completed.

firestore.reasoning:
The Firestore data structure is designed to support the Code Conqueror application, prioritizing security, scalability, and debuggability by adhering to the principles of Authorization Independence, Clarity of Intent, DBAC (Database-Based Access Control), and QAPs (Rules are not Filters). Authorization Independence is achieved through denormalization, copying relevant authorization data (e.g., roles) into subcollections to avoid `get()` calls in security rules. Structural Segregation ensures that each collection has a homogeneous security posture, simplifying rules. Access Modeling employs consistent patterns like path-based ownership for private user data and membership maps for collaborative data.

Specifically:

*   User profiles are stored under `/users/{userId}`, ensuring private data is easily secured using path-based rules. Certificates are stored in a subcollection `/users/{userId}/certificates/{certificateId}`, inheriting ownership from the user profile.
*   Courses and Badges are stored in root-level collections `/courses` and `/badges` respectively, as they are globally accessible entities.
*   Levels and Games are nested under Courses to reflect their hierarchical relationship, enabling structured data access and management.

QAPs (Rules are not Filters) is addressed through structural segregation. List operations are secured based on path-based ownership for user-specific data and by granting read access to all authenticated users for global data such as Courses and Badges.
